1.title: Foundations: complexity, arrays, linked lists, stacks

Complexity.outcome: Compare algorithms using Big-O notation and common growth rates
Complexity.why: Every later data-structure choice is justified by its time cost.

Arrays.outcome: Explain contiguous storage and the cost of indexing and insertion
Arrays.why: Arrays underlie strings, matrices, heaps and hash tables.

Linked Lists.outcome: Describe node-based storage and compare list operations with array operations
Linked Lists.why: Pointer-based structures are the base for stacks, queues, trees and graphs.

Stacks.outcome: Apply LIFO behaviour and stack operations to problems such as call management
Stacks.why: Stacks power recursion, expression evaluation and undo features.

Queues.outcome: Apply FIFO behaviour, queue operations and the circular queue idea
Queues.why: Queues drive scheduling, buffering and breadth-first traversal.

Trees.outcome: Define binary trees and BSTs and describe traversals and basic properties
Trees.why: Trees model hierarchies and give efficient search structures.

Sorting.outcome: Compare common sorting algorithms by complexity and stability
Sorting.why: Sorting is a building block of searching and many other algorithms.

Searching.outcome: Apply linear and binary search and state their requirements and costs
Searching.why: Choosing the right search method decides how fast data can be found.
